decisions.reason: As a close extension of the firm's integrated airport operations software, it now benefits from another year of learning with existing customers, making continued improvement more likely than withdrawal.
Because this module builds directly on the firm's apron integration knowledge and installed customer base, absorptive capacity remains strong and supports keeping it in the portfolio.

Revenue calculation and billing software is less central to the firm's operational core, but it still draws on the same airport data and software capabilities, so management would likely retain it while monitoring strategic fit.
Apron equipment monitoring is closely tied to the firm's maintenance, installed-base, and analytics capabilities, so accumulated operational feedback favors further development rather than exit.

The controller safety alert service fits the firm's safety-critical systems expertise and in-house R&D profile, and although adoption may be gradual, it remains sufficiently aligned to justify continuation.
